record.paper_title: Developments and open problems on chiral polytopes
record.original_question: Does every convex regular polytope admit a chiral extension?

evidence.quote: Problem 30 Does every convex regular polytope admit a chiral extensions?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract polytope of rank d is a partially ordered set with a strictly monotone rank function onto {-1, 0, 1, ..., d}, with a unique minimum face (of rank -1) and a unique maximum face (of rank d), in which every maximal chain (flag) has exactly d+2 elements, which is strongly flag-connected, and which satisfies the diamond condition: whenever F < G with rank(G) = rank(F) + 2, there are exactly two faces H with F < H < G. The automorphism group of such a polytope acts on its flags; the polytope is called regular if this action is transitive, and chiral if the automorphism group has exactly two orbits on flags such that any two adjacent flags lie in different orbits. Given an abstract polytope K of rank d, a chiral extension of K is a chiral abstract polytope P of rank d+1 all of whose facets (faces of rank d) are isomorphic to K. The convex regular polytopes are the classical regular polytopes in Euclidean space: in rank 3, the five Platonic solids; in rank 4, the six convex regular 4-polytopes (5-cell, 8-cell, 16-cell, 24-cell, 120-cell, 600-cell); and in rank d ≥ 5, the d-simplex, the d-cube, and the d-cross-polytope. Each such convex regular polytope determines an abstract regular polytope via its face lattice.

Question: Does every convex regular polytope, viewed as an abstract regular polytope, admit a chiral extension?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears to remain open. Subsequent work (Cunningham–Pellicer on chiral extensions of chiral polytopes; Montero–Toledo on chiral extensions of regular toroids; Montero on Schläfli symbols of chiral extensions) has produced chiral extensions in many cases—e.g., chiral d-polytopes for every d ≥ 3, and chiral extensions of regular cubic tessellations of the n-torus—but no source found resolves the question for all convex regular polytopes (in particular, no general construction or obstruction is reported covering the full list of Platonic solids, the six convex regular 4-polytopes, and the d-simplex/d-cube/d-cross-polytope for all d).

status_evidence.title: Chiral Extensions of Regular Toroids (Montero–Toledo)
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of chiral polytopes whose facets are isomorphic to a prescribed regular cubic tessellation of the n-dimensional torus; consequence: chiral d-polytopes exist for every d ≥ 3.
status_evidence.claim: Recent results establish chiral extensions for specific families of regular polytopes (toroids), but not for all convex regular polytopes.

status_evidence.title: On the Schläfli symbol of chiral extensions of polytopes (Montero)
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs chiral extensions of dually bipartite chiral polytopes with regular facets with arbitrarily large last Schläfli entry.
status_evidence.claim: Partial constructions of chiral extensions exist, addressing related but not identical questions.

status_evidence.title: Chiral extensions of chiral polytopes (Cunningham–Pellicer)
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs chiral (d+1)-polytope P with facets isomorphic to a given chiral d-polytope K with regular facets.
status_evidence.claim: Existing extension theorems target chiral (not all regular) facets, leaving the convex-regular case unresolved.
